clue.text: Line 5 is the thing — otherwise a social worker

parts.note: the District line is one of the London Underground lines
clue 5 gives STOP, and someone who stops (stays) at a place is a visitor, the thing that does so

explanation.surface: A muddled description of a London Tube line that turns out to be a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle is themed on London Underground lines. '5' points to the answer of 5 down, STOP: one who stops with you is a visitor, so the District line's 'stopper' is a DISTRICT VISITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A district visitor was a parish volunteer who called on the poor and sick, an early form of social work.

parts.note: the Metropolitan line is a London Underground line

explanation.surface: A railway line at an Eastern Church sounds like a posting for a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern Church' looks like one phrase, but Eastern only gives E and Church belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolitanate is the office or see of a metropolitan, a senior archbishop, so it is a church post.

clue.text: Device useful to umpires came across in barge

indicators.note: in tells us one word is placed inside the other, the meeting put within the boat

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for loading ships
came across means met, encountered

explanation.surface: Someone encountered a gadget for cricket umpires while aboard a barge.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, umpires use a light meter to decide whether bad light should stop play.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic exposure gauge measures brightness, which umpires consult to judge whether play is safe.

parts.note: Tex is a stock nickname for a Texan cowboy
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Asking what fabric a cowboy's hat is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' for a hat is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Any woven fabric or cloth counts as a textile.

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word for large quantities is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: pots means large quantities, as in pots of money

explanation.surface: Big amounts are lifted up at a railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop is a place where a train or bus halts, i.e. a station on the line.

clue.text: Wrong right in two acts with line — one round pole

indicators.note: wrong signals that these letters are put into the wrong order
two asks for the word for acts to appear twice

parts.note: an act is a deed, the noun acts giving act
the Circle line is a London Underground line

explanation.surface: A garbled play-review: wrong right, two acts and a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges R, IN and ACTACT into ANTARCTIC; the Circle line then completes the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antarctic Circle is the line of latitude encircling the South Pole, one ring round a pole.

indicators.note: incorrectly says these letters are put together the wrong way round, as a new arrangement

parts.note: the answer to 4 down is TEXTILE, so 4s is its plural

explanation.surface: Wondering about the straightness of fabrics, and told you have misheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' suggests a sound-alike, but it is fodder: TEXTILES plus YOU and HEAR are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight is slang for heterosexual, so straightness is the quality of being heterosexual.

parts.note: shoots a gun means fires
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.definitionFit: The fireside is the hearth, standing for home and domestic life.

clue.text: Melody containing new line to hold most of these lines

definitions.text: to hold most of these lines

indicators.note: containing means the tune holds the new letter inside it

parts.note: a melody is a tune

explanation.surface: A tune that includes a new line, meant to contain most of these lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'These lines' are the Tube lines of the theme, which mostly run underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Most London Underground routes run through bored tubes, so a tunnel holds them.

parts.note: a brilliant performer is a star
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A dazzling friend owns something to stiffen a collar.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is applied to laundry to make it rigid, so it is a stiffening agent.

clue.text: When Tyler comes in, gradually reduce basic drink

indicators.note: comes in means the rebel's name goes inside the word for narrowing

parts.note: taper means to diminish gradually
Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381

explanation.surface: A man named Tyler arrives as someone cuts back to the simplest drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler was the leader of the 1381 Peasants' Revolt in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Water straight from the tap is the most ordinary, unadorned drink.

definitions.meaning: 10 across is STARCH, and something floppy that needs stiffening is ...

explanation.definitionFit: Limping is lame walking, and a limp collar is one lacking the stiffness that starch gives.

parts.note: a fellow is a man, a male
in Scotland a factor manages a landed estate

explanation.surface: A crooked man who runs the estate.
explanation.walkthrough: A factor is the Scottish term for a land agent running an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer, someone who commits crimes.

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of two words are swapped, as Rev Spooner did

parts.note: straw describes something worthless, as in a man of straw
folk are people

explanation.surface: Spooner talks of good-for-nothings involved in burning.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the sounds of STRAW FOLK gives FOUR STROKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-stroke engine runs a four-stage internal combustion cycle, so it names a type of combustion.

clue.text: In the presence of death let everyone be a sporting type

indicators.note: in the presence of says the answer is present within these words

explanation.surface: A deathbed instruction to let everyone be sporty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the presence of' looks like AT, but the answer sits whole in deATH LET Everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is someone who plays sport, a sporting kind of person.

definitions.meaning: the ... line is a London Underground line
a golden anniversary celebration comes after fifty years

explanation.definitionFit: The Jubilee line is a Tube route, and a fiftieth anniversary is a golden celebration.

clue.text: Girl in grass plot round sundial, she hopes!

indicators.note: in places the girl's name within the Jabberwocky word

parts.note: Humpty Dumpty explains the wabe in Jabberwocky as the grass plot round a sundial
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl in the lawn round a sundial, full of hope.
explanation.walkthrough: In Through the Looking-Glass, Humpty Dumpty glosses 'wabe' from Jabberwocky as the grass plot round a sundial.
explanation.definitionFit: A wannabe is an aspirant who hopes to become something, so 'she hopes' describes one.

parts.note: the Victoria line is a London Underground line
N is north, the first pole
S is south, the second pole

explanation.surface: A railway line laid over the poles in the 1800s.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorians are people who lived in Queen Victoria's reign, most of the nineteenth century.

definitions.meaning: a heavy stick used to hit
one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.definitionFit: A club is a cudgel, and clubs is one of the card suits.

clue.text: Spicy stuff to read outside pub before lunch

indicators.note: outside means the word for study goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to con is to study or read carefully
an inn is a pub
am means morning, the time before lunch

explanation.surface: Reading outdoors at the pub before a midday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnamon is an aromatic spice from tree bark.

definitions.meaning: the setter speaking of his own, belonging to me
a pit dug to extract coal or ore

explanation.definitionFit: Mine is the possessive for something belonging to me, and a mine is a dug pit.

clue.text: It's not often you find an artist to trust

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to rely on is to trust

explanation.surface: It's seldom you meet a painter you can depend on.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means seldom, only on infrequent occasions.

clue.text: Bike burnt by Eliot makes line for the Irish

definitions.meaning: Burnt ... is the first of T S Eliot's Four Quartets
the Northern line said in an Irish accent, with th as t

explanation.definitionFit: Norton made motorcycles, Eliot wrote Burnt Norton, and an Irish voice says Northern this way.

clue.text: Line, half of it and not much of that, forms resistant stuff

indicators.note: half of it means only the first half of the line's name is taken

parts.note: the Bakerloo line is a London Underground line
lite describes a reduced, low-strength version of something, not much of it

explanation.surface: A recipe of a line, half of it and only a little of that, makes something tough.
explanation.walkthrough: Halve BAKERLOO to BAKE, then add LITE, the light version of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakelite is an early plastic prized for resisting heat and electricity.
